## Overview

Site presentations are a crucial part of sections. Site presentations allow everyone to set their expectations (or hopes!) of what the field trip will entail the next day.

You will be responsible for briefing your peers for _one_ site. Sign up for a site presentation [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1OR393YzaPTC-R-mELllMHuMeYUTgz5k1FTE8WXMv8Uk/edit?usp=sharing).

## Your responsibilities

Prior to giving your site presentation, you should:

- [ ] complete any readings on Canvas
- [ ] read the chapter relating to your site's ecosystem and/or management from _Ecosystems of California_
- [ ] coordinate with your site presentation partner on: 
  - [ ] how you would like to work together on your presentation
  - [ ] when you would like to meet with An to check in about your presentation
- [ ] explore observations from your site on iNaturalist and eBird
  
:::{.callout-tip title="_Ecosystems of California_"}
Much of the ecological information you will need to digest and relay to your peers is in _Ecosystems of California_ (edited by Harold Mooney and Erika Zavaleta). The book can be accessed online via the [UCSB Library](https://search.library.ucsb.edu/permalink/01UCSB_INST/1o0vcsa/alma9912432923906531) for **free**. To access the book, you must be connected to the campus wireless network, logged in via the library proxy, or connected to a campus VPN. See An if you need help with any of these options.
:::

## What to include

All site presentations should be in the form of Google or Powerpoint slides. Your presentation should include:

- [ ] the site name
- [ ] the dominant ecosystem type (this can be tricky to categorize, )
